t: No part of any appropriation under this Act shall be available to the Secretaries of the Interior and Agriculture for use for any sale hereafter made of unprocessed timber from Federal lands west of the 100th meridian in the contiguous 48 States which will be exported from the United States, or which will be used as a substitute for timber from private lands which is exported by the purchaser: Provided, That this limitation shall not apply to specific quantities of grades and species of timber which said Secretaries determine are surplus to domestic lumber and plywood manufacturing needs.

fable.w: This is an appropriations limitation barring the use of funds for sales of unprocessed federal timber that will be exported, with an exception for timber the Secretaries find surplus. The tempting reading is that the surplus determination or the reference to purchasers and private lands brings in outside parties, but the determination is made solely by the Secretaries of the Interior and Agriculture. The section requires no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue.
fable.s: Provided, That this limitation shall not apply to specific quantities of grades and species of timber which said Secretaries determine are surplus to domestic lumber and plywood manufacturing needs.

qwen_block.w: This section restricts the use of federal appropriations for timber sales and grants the Secretaries of the Interior and Agriculture the authority to make a determination regarding surplus timber. There is no requirement or recommendation for consultation with outside parties, public comment, or advisory boards. The decision-making process is entirely internal to the federal executive branch.
qwen_block.s: Provided, That this limitation shall not apply to specific quantities of grades and species of timber which said Secretaries determine are surplus to domestic lumber and plywood manufacturing needs.

opus.w: This is a limit on how appropriated funds may be used for timber sales. The only decision it describes is the Secretaries deciding which timber is surplus, and they make that call themselves, without consulting anyone outside the federal government. It might seem tempting to count the timber purchasers or the Secretaries' surplus finding as participation, but buying timber is a commercial deal, and the finding is a decision made inside the government with no comment period, hearing, or outside consultation.
opus.s: Provided, That this limitation shall not apply to specific quantities of grades and species of timber which said Secretaries determine are surplus to domestic lumber and plywood manufacturing needs.

qwen_chat.w: The section grants the Secretaries of the Interior and Agriculture the authority to determine whether certain timber is surplus to domestic needs. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties (such as industry, states, or the public) in making that determination. The decision-making process described is entirely internal to the federal executive branch.
qwen_chat.s: Provided, That this limitation shall not apply to specific quantities of grades and species of timber which said Secretaries determine are surplus to domestic lumber and plywood manufacturing needs.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the Secretaries' determination of "surplus" timber involves consultation with industry or the public, but the text does not mandate or even suggest such consultation. It simply grants the Secretaries the authority to make that determination. There is no mention of hearings, comments, advisory boards, or coordination with outside entities.
